## Motivation
Enable XPU execution of the DeepSeek V4/4.1 FP4 indexer by integrating the corresponding SYCL operators from sgl-kernel-xpu.
The SYCL implementations are added in the `sgl-kernel-xpu` PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/572) and exposed as
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_fp4_quant`, `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fp4_paged_mqa_logits`, `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.index_q_rope_pack_weights`, `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.index_k_norm_rope_pack_store`.

## Modifications
Enable FP4 indexer configuration on XPU

Allow --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer on XPU devices.
Update platform validation and the associated error message.
Integrate DeepSeek V4 FP4 query preparation and scoring

Dispatch fused query RoPE, Hadamard transform, and FP4 quantization to sgl_kernel.fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_fp4_quant.
Convert the complex RoPE cache to the real-valued layout expected by the SYCL operator.
Reinterpret per-group scale bytes as packed int32 scales to preserve the caller-facing layout.
Dispatch paged FP4 MQA logits to sgl_kernel.fp4_paged_mqa_logits on XPU instead of DeepGEMM.
Integrate DeepSeek V4.1 Q/K preparation

Use sgl_kernel.index_q_rope_pack_weights for query RoPE, FP4 packing, and head-weight preparation.
Use sgl_kernel.index_k_norm_rope_pack_store for fused key RMSNorm, RoPE, FP4 packing, and paged-cache storage in the applicable decode/target-verify and extend paths.
Preserve existing platform paths

Select XPU operators through platform-specific dispatch.
Keep CUDA and ROCm implementations unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Correctness of the XPU dispatch is verified against the
PyTorch reference at the kernel level in the `sgl-kernel-xpu` PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/572)

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+"""C4Indexer.compute_q's XPU FP4 path against the real sgl_kernel op.
+
+Kernel numerics are tested in sgl-kernel-xpu; this guards the sglang side of
+the contract: the XPU branch must return the same layout as the CUDA
+``fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_fp4_quant`` (int8 payload, packed int32
+scales, float32 fused weights), fed compute_q's real tensors.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_xpu
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not is_xpu(), reason="XPU required")
+
+DEVICE = "xpu"
+ROWS, HEADS, HEAD_DIM, MAX_POS = 3, 4, 128, 16
+
+
+def test_compute_q_fp4_allocations_accepted_by_kernel():
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4.indexer import C4Indexer
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    indexer = object.__new__(C4Indexer)
+    indexer.use_fp4_indexer = True
+    indexer.n_local_heads = HEADS
+    indexer.head_dim = HEAD_DIM
+    indexer.weight_scale = 0.25
+    # The kernel reads the rope cache as real float32 [MAX_POS, 64].
+    indexer.freqs_cis = torch.randn(
+        MAX_POS, 32, dtype=torch.complex64, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    q = torch.randn(
+        ROWS, HEADS * HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    indexer.wq_b = lambda q_lora: (q, None)
+    weight = torch.randn(ROWS, HEADS, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    positions = torch.randint(0, MAX_POS, (ROWS,), device=DEVICE)
+
+    # The real kernel wrapper allocates the outputs and TORCH_CHECKs dtypes;
+    # with the earlier uint8 q_fp4 regression this raised "q_fp4 must be int8".
+    (q_fp4, q_scale), weights = indexer.compute_q(object(), positions, weight)
+
+    # Callers consume the CUDA kernel's layout: int8 payload and one packed
+    # int32 ue8m0 scale per (token, head).
+    assert q_fp4.dtype == torch.int8
+    assert q_fp4.shape == (ROWS, HEADS, HEAD_DIM // 2)
+    assert q_scale.dtype == torch.int32
+    assert q_scale.shape == (ROWS, HEADS)
+    assert weights.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert weights.shape == (ROWS, HEADS, 1)
+    # The kernel actually wrote: ue8m0 exponent bytes are never all zero for
+    # gaussian inputs, and the fused weights must be finite.
+    assert q_scale.view(torch.uint8).count_nonzero() > 0
+    assert torch.isfinite(weights).all()

inline_comments.body:
`q_fp4` is allocated as `torch.uint8`, but the paired SYCL kernel explicitly requires `at::kChar` (`torch.int8`), so the first invocation fails with `q_fp4 must be int8 and q_scale must be uint8`. See the [kernel dtype check](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/blob/c2e25e98423a3e4e4e0436dfb6b2e5fc5c8beb38/src/sycl/FusedQIndexerRopeHadamardFp4Quant.cpp#L194).

Please allocate `q_fp4` as `torch.int8` and add an adapter-level regression test; the kernel-only tests do not exercise this allocation.
